Refactored the B-tree around a single in-order traversal primitive so the internal organization is less duplicated and easier to extend. `BTree` now exposes `isEmpty()`, `forEachKey(IntConsumer)`, `toList()`, and `toString()`, all built on the same node walk instead of maintaining separate traversal and formatting paths ([BTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTree.java:30), [BTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTree.java:34), [BTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTree.java:41), [BTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTree.java:72), [BTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTree.java:129)). That reduces internal coupling and makes new read-only views easier to add later.

I also cleaned up the demo to rely on the tree’s string representation instead of having the data structure own console formatting ([Main.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/Main.java:5)). To support future refactors, I added a small regression harness in [BTreeTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeTest.java:4) covering constructor validation, empty-tree behavior, sorted traversal, and membership checks.
